caption: Co- Regulation.
author: Chris Lee - Nervous System Tools and Strategies
transcript: In case you didn't know, you can co-regulate with somebody. When you're stressed out and somebody is regulated, you can kind of piggyback off their nervous system state and help you get grounded when you're stressed out. It also works the other way, and that's because there's an area of your brain called the fusiform gyrus, and a huge chunk of its responsibility is to look at other people's faces and body language and kind of adapt to the state of the collective that you're spending time with. So if you're hanging out with people who are stressed, burnt out, dishonest, like don't have integrity, your system is going to constantly be on edge trying to figure out and narrow down where the damage can be done. So yes, it is way more cost effective to not only say, yeah, I'm not going, but to start to cut those people out of your life, either with boundaries or just being able to say no. One of the greatest social regulation strategies is very simple, hard to miss, can't forget it. No. It's just saying no. Not only does it reserve your own resources, because I think burnout is the manifestation of stealing resources tomorrow to meet today's needs, but it also, you're going to start to recognize this, starts to help you better understand what you are and are not willing to tolerate. And exhaustion from people who are not taking care of themselves is one of those things.
title: Co-Regulation: Why Your Circle Shapes Your Nervous System
one_liner: Your brain mirrors others' states, so stressed company keeps your nervous system on edge.
key_points: The fusiform gyrus reads faces and body language, adapting your nervous system to match those around you
Surrounding yourself with dysregulated people keeps your system in constant threat-detection mode
Saying 'no' conserves internal resources and prevents burnout, which is borrowing from tomorrow to meet today's needs
Cutting out or setting boundaries with draining people is a legitimate nervous system regulation strategy
